newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin moves to hunting lodge before Kohl talks.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin moves to hunting lodge before Kohl talks.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin moved on Friday to the Rus state hunting lodge near Moscow to prepare for a meeting there on Saturday with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.

A presidential spokesman said Yeltsin, who returned to the Kremlin two weeks ago after his heart bypass operation on November 5, flew by helicopter from Moscow to the residence at Zavidovo, 100 km (60 miles) west of the capital.

Kohl, who regards himself as a personal friend of Yeltsin, will be the first Western leader to meet the 65-year-old Russian president since he underwent surgery. The chancellor last met Yeltsin in September, also at Rus.

One item will dominate the agenda -- NATO's plan to admit east European states while forming a special relationship with Russia in an effort to overcome its strong objections to the enlargement of the Atlantic alliance.
German government spokesman Herbert Schmuelling told journalists on Friday that the future shape of the European security system would be the main topic of the three or four hours of talks.

Kohl will be hoping his warm personal relations with Yeltsin and the close ties Germany has with Russia -- Bonn is Moscow's biggest creditor -- can help advance the compromise both NATO and Russia say they want to see this year.

After often divergent statements from Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov, Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and Security Council secretary Ivan Rybkin, Kohl and other Western leaders may be seeking assurances that Yeltsin's return means a more coordinated and predictable stance from Russia.

There is a special personal chemistry between Kohl and Yeltsin. In September, Yeltsin invited the German leader to take a brief Siberian holiday with him in 1997, promising to share the joys of the traditional Russian "banya" or steam bath.

French President Jacques Chirac is also due in Moscow later this month and President Bill Clinton plans to meet Yeltsin in the United States in March. British Prime Minister John Major has also had an invitation to Russia but a date is yet to be set.
Apart from discussing NATO, Kohl may urge Yeltsin to push ahead with creating safer and more stable conditions to help overcome Western companies' continuing fears about investing in Russia.
Schmuelling said the two would also discuss the situation in the Middle East and Yugoslavia.
Another German source said Kohl might raise the vexed question of repatriation of hoards of art taken to Russia by the invading Red Army as booty at the end of World War Two.
